title: What to Expect in Markets This Week: Nvidia Earnings; Software Firms, Discount Stores Also Report
excerpt: The world’s most valuable publicly-traded company is slated to share results on Wednesday afternoon.
content_html:
Sarina Trangle

Sun, August 23, 2026 at 4:00 AM MDT 4 min read

Anxious about Nvidia's results? You're likely not alone.

The stock sold off in the wake of its last three quarterly reports. Another re-evaluation could come Wednesday, when the world's most valuable company hands in its second-quarter results.

The AI chipmaker has had an active summer. CEO Jensen Huang announced a new chip purpose-built to power on-device AI agents, while the company made progress on its attempts to sell chips in China, and struck deals to help finance the AI data center buildout. The stock, meanwhile, has had a volatile year, but it's mostly risen, up 15% in 2025 though off its May highs.

Last quarter, Nvidia beat expectations and brightened its outlook, with Huang saying demand "has gone parabolic" as companies race to build AI infrastructure. Revenue climbed 85% year-over-year, with data center sales nearly doubling.

There's a lot riding on Nvidia's performance. For every $1 it collects, another $8 to $10 is spent on other technology, according to Wedbush estimates. Much of the economy and stock market's recent growth has been driven by tech giants building AI data centers, pouring money into chips, memory and data storage technology, energy infrastructure and even construction equipment. The investment is so big that the Federal Reserve is monitoring its impact on inflation. 

Other segments of the economy will also get some attention this week. A number of software companies report, including CrowdStrike, Intuit and Salesforce, as well as discount stores, beauty retailers and apparel companies like Gap, Abercrombie & Fitch and Kohl's.

Market Recap

The major stock indexes fell this week as investors scrutinized bond yields and doubts mounted that the U.S. would reach a deal with Iran. The yield on 30-year Treasury bonds hit levels not seen since 2007 amid concerns about inflation and government debt, though yields temporarily reversed their trajectory when the Treasury announced it would buy back more long-term debt. For more detail on last week's trading, read Friday's market recap here.

This Week's Top Events

Here's a look at major events in the week ahead. TradingView publishes a more detailed calendar, but clicking the link will take you off the Investopedia site.

  • Tuesday, Aug. 25: Intuit (INTU) is slated to publish its fiscal fourth-quarter results after the closing bell and host a conference call at 4:30 p.m. ET. The parent company of TurboTax and QuickBooks beat expectations last quarter and announced plans to shrink its workforce.

  • Wednesday, Aug. 26: The Bureau of Economic Analysis is due to publish the July Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index at 8:30 a.m. ET. The cost-of-living index rose 3.7% year-over-year in June, down from 4.1% in May. Other inflation trackers also show inflation has cooled, but the Federal Reserve uses PCE as its benchmark.

  • Wednesday: Kohl's (KSS) is set to host a conference call on its results at 9 a.m. ET, with the numbers expected before then. The department store said earlier this year it was focusing on $10-and-under items and drawing attention to deals on the sales floor. Kohl's launched a turnaround campaign in 2025 as bargain retailers, including Burlington Stores (BURL) made inroads with shoppers. Burlington reports before markets open on Thursday.

  • Wednesday: Nvidia (NVDA) is slated to publish its results at 4:20 p.m. ET, followed by a conference call at 5 p.m. ET. 

  • Wednesday: CrowdStrike (CRWD) is set to release its results after the market closes and host a conference call at 5 p.m. ET. The cybersecurity firm beat expectations last quarter. Analysts have signaled that they see AI expanding demand for cybersecurity software companies, including SentinelOne (S), which reports after the close on Thursday. 

  • Wednesday: Salesforce (CRM) is set to release its results after the closing bell and host a conference call at 5 p.m. ET. The software company handed in strong numbers last quarter, but its guidance disappointed investors.

  • Thursday, Aug. 27: Best Buy (BBY) is scheduled to host a conference call on its results at 8 a.m. ET, with the numbers expected before then. The electronics retailer is in the midst of a leadership transition and has launched a digital marketplace as it tries to revive sales.

  • Thursday: Dollar General (DG) is slated to release its results and host a conference call at 9 a.m. ET. The discount store posted better-than-expected profit last quarter and raised its outlook. Dollar Tree (DLTR) also reports on Thursday morning.

  • Thursday: Gap Inc. (GAP) is scheduled to publish its results at 4:15 p.m. ET, followed by a conference call at 5 p.m. ET. The company trimmed its outlook last quarter. Peers Abercrombie & Fitch (ANF) and Urban Outfitters (URBN) are both slated to report on Wednesday.

  • Thursday: Ulta Beauty (ULTA) plans to release its results after the closing bell and host a webcast and conference call at 4:30 p.m. ET. Shares of the beauty company slipped after each of its earnings reports earlier this year. Bath & Body Works (BBWI) reports on Wednesday morning.

  • Thursday: Marvell Technology (MRVL) is set to release its second-quarter results and hold a conference call at 4:45 p.m. ET. The AI chip designer recently joined the S&P 500 and received a shout-out from Nvidia's Huang, who said Marvell could be "the next trillion-dollar company."

  • Friday, Aug. 28: Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh is expected to speak at the Jackson Hole Symposium, where he could discuss the economy and the interplay between the Fed and bond market, per CNBC.

Other segments of the economy will also get some attention this week. A number of software companies report, including CrowdStrike, Intuit and Salesforce, as well as discount stores, beauty retailers and apparel companies like Gap, Abercrombie & Fitch and Kohl's.

市场回顾

The major stock indexes fell this week as investors scrutinized bond yields and doubts mounted that the U.S. would reach a deal with Iran. The yield on 30-year Treasury bonds hit levels not seen since 2007 amid concerns about inflation and government debt, though yields temporarily reversed their trajectory when the Treasury announced it would buy back more long-term debt.
